tier_reason: Upgraded C to A: benchmark code is public (Main.cpp, CLog.cpp, build_m.bat at the repo root), the README gives the exact MSVC command lines (cl -DNDEBUG -Ox -EHsc) and the CPU (Core i7-8700 3.20GHz), and the raw timings behind the bar charts are checked in as Benchmark/c*_*.txt and fill_c*_*.txt. MSVC version is not stated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Raw totals in Benchmark/*.txt (seconds, lower is better, 8 threads, alloc+free only): 0B-1KiB KanameShiki 1.73 vs MSVC malloc 2.33, mimalloc 1.90, jemalloc 2.99, tcmalloc 15.35; 2KiB-32KiB 0.58 vs malloc 3.27, mimalloc 2.31, jemalloc 1.13; 64KiB-1MiB 0.33 vs malloc 27.59, jemalloc 0.60; 2MiB-32MiB 3.22 vs malloc 89.80, mimalloc 49.26, jemalloc 5.35. With memory fill, 0B-1KiB 8 threads: 2.29 vs malloc 2.82, mimalloc 2.53; 2MiB-32MiB 8 threads: 3730.7 vs malloc 6186.0, mimalloc 3085.8 (mimalloc faster but it had 230,000 allocation failures). Single thread 0B-1KiB: 0.036 vs malloc 0.151 but slower than mimalloc 0.022 and tcmalloc 0.029.
corrections.caveats: Windows-only published results against the MSVC CRT heap; MSVC version not stated. Alloc+free-only large-block tests show implausible gaps (single-thread 2MiB-32MiB: 0.006 s vs malloc 17.0 s, about 2800x derived from page data), likely from caching freed blocks instead of returning them to the OS; with memory fill the gap shrinks to about 1.66x vs malloc and mimalloc is faster. The c4_1.txt rows are labelled KanameShiki0_4.exe/KanameShiki1_4.exe (copy-paste labelling). Author says jemalloc segfaulted frequently on the MSVC build and mimalloc had 230,000 allocation failures in the 2MiB-32MiB test; Mingw64 builds do not work; last commit 2019-10-19.

notes: README charts hide numbers, but the Benchmark/ directory holds the raw text results, so the speedups are quotable. Tier A is mechanical (code, flags, CPU stated); the orchestrator may prefer to note the large-block alloc-only rows as unrepresentative.

tier_reason: First-party benchmark code (memplusplus-benchmarks: benchmark_alloc.cpp, benchmark_complex.cpp, etc.) with results only as box-plot images; no compiler flags or CPU stated, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Charts only (values read off the plots, approximate): allocating 4096 random-size objects mem++ about 590 us vs jemalloc about 1160 us and mimalloc about 960 us, but slower than ptmalloc2 (glibc 2.31) about 220 us and rpmalloc about 150-200 us. Complex 1M-op benchmark: mem++ about 1010 ms vs jemalloc about 2000 ms and rpmalloc about 1340 ms, but slower than mimalloc about 670 ms and ptmalloc2 about 700 ms. README: heap compaction improves linked-list iteration 4-8x versus its own randomized layout.
corrections.caveats: Slower than glibc malloc (ptmalloc2) in both the allocation and the complex benchmark shown; wins only against jemalloc and rpmalloc in some charts. No LICENSE file in the repo (license unknown, reference only). Headline 4-8x is against its own uncompacted layout. Single-threaded only; README says not for production; hardware and compiler flags not stated; numbers only as images.

notes: Kept as C; the orchestrator may want a not-faster-than-glibc shortcoming, since ptmalloc2 beats it on both charted timing benchmarks.

tier_reason: md/benchmarks.md compares against glibc 2.17, jemalloc 5.3.0, mimalloc 1.8 and snmalloc 3.14 with gcc 10.3.0 on a Xeon Gold 5220R, and the benchs/ code is public, but compiler flags are not stated and results are plots only, so C.
notes: Page text matches the record: lower memory overhead, faster than glibc (which scales negatively with threads), slower than snmalloc and jemalloc. Metadata (MIT, 33 stars, last commit 2024-11-14) matches.
